subject: Supply-chain onboarding: subprocessor ownership & evidence sprint
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@hearthhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Supply-chain onboarding: subprocessor ownership & evidence sprint

Hi Sofia / HearthHealth procurement team,

Thanks for the heads-up on the onboarding timeline. Per your ask, we'd like to kick off a short evidence sprint so your GRC reviewers have the subprocessor residency, KMS ownership, and SOC/CAIQ artifacts in one bundle.

Attached is a lightweight manifest template (redwood_subprocessor_manifest_v1.xlsx) that we use to enumerate each subprocessor, data flows, residency, and control owners. For your immediate questions we can provide:
- SOC 2 Type II (we've attached the 2026 report)
- CAIQ responses (we'll export a CSV for your tracker)
- KMS residency matrix and key custody notes

Can you confirm the internal reviewers and an ideal due date for the initial bundle? We can target EOD Tue (2027-05-25) for a first pass if that works.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm reviewers & any outstanding evidence types (e.g., export-control attestation).
2) Our team fills the manifest & drops artifacts to a shared Drive link.
3) We run a short call to walk the bundle and answer follow-up items.

Thanks — happy to adjust cadence.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_manifest_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB), SOC2-TypeII-redwood-2026.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@hearthhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Supply-chain onboarding: subprocessor ownership & evidence sprint

Thanks Laura — this looks good and the timeline is reasonable. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) KMS residency: our policy requires a clear statement of which keys are customer-dedicated vs service-managed (including HSM/KMS provider and region). Can you confirm which subprocessor components hold customer key material?

2) Export-control / residency: HearthHealth requires evidence of EU/UK residency for any subprocessors that process EU patient pseudonymized datasets. If a subprocessor can only promise contractual safeguards and not physical residency, note that explicitly.

3) CAIQ: can you provide a completed CAIQ CSV for your current production release (we call this "CAIQ 2027-Q2"). We'll import it into our vendor portal.

Reviewers: myself (GRC), + Procurement (procurement@hearthhealth.com), and our Legal lead, Miguel Torres (miguel.torres@hearthhealth.com). Initial target date of 2027-05-25 works for a first pass; final acceptance will likely take an additional 5 business days.

If you can include a short KMS custody diagram (where keys are generated, stored, and who has ability to rotate/revoke), that will expedite review.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
GRC Manager, HearthHealth
sofia.martinez@hearthhealth.com

Laura / Grace — forwarding Sofia's note. Quick responses inline so we can commit owners: 

> 1) KMS residency: our policy requires a clear statement of which keys are customer-dedicated vs service-managed (including HSM/KMS provider and region). Can you confirm which subprocessor components hold customer key material?

We have three relevant pieces:
- Customer-data envelope keys: customer-dedicated, generated in the customer's VPC via AWS KMS (us-east-1) when on Redwood Private. For Hosted customers we provide envelope keys managed in our HSM cluster (AWS CloudHSM us-east-1) but with per-customer wrapping keys.
- Runtime signing keys (non-customer secrets): service-managed, rotated by infra weekly, stored in HashiCorp Vault (GCP us-central1 for dedicated pools).
- Telemetry/export keys (log shipping): service-managed, rotated monthly.

I'll draft a one-page KMS custody diagram and a short table mapping each subprocessor component to residency. Mina — can you own the manifest population for the first pass?

Grace — please confirm whether SOC artifacts require an NDA/proprietary flag before we share (I believe the SOC2 redacted report is shareable).

Jonas
Director, Infrastructure Security
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround and the reviewer list. Per Jonas / Mina's notes below, attached is the initial bundle for your intake team:

- redwood_subprocessor_manifest_v1.xlsx (populated)
- KMS_residency_matrix.pdf (high-level custody diagram + region table)
- SOC2-TypeII-redwood-2026.pdf (redacted; standard distribution)
- CAIQ_responses_2027.csv (export of our CAIQ answers)

Call to action: can Procurement / GRC confirm receipt and let us know any high-priority gaps by EOD 2027-05-27? We'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on 2027-05-28 (proposed: 10:00am PT).

Notes & caveats:
- For customers on Redwood Private (VPC), we guarantee customer-dedicated envelope keys generated inside their cloud tenancy. For hosted accounts we use a per-customer wrapping model with HSM-backed storage; the manifest clarifies per-subprocessor whether keys are service-managed or customer-managed.
- Some subprocessor residency (third-party analytics) is contractual only and not physically resident in EU. Those rows are flagged in the manifest and include contractual mitigations.

If you need us to redline anything in the manifest or provide an export-control statement, loop in your legal contact and we'll supply a short attestation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
